classification.difficultyReason: Interpret 45 km south as a component of the journey, convert the bearing to 24 degrees from south and construct the right triangle. Recognise the journey as the hypotenuse and rearrange the cosine equation.

content.prompt: A ship sails on a bearing of $156^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ until it is $45\text{ km}$ south of its starting point. How far has it travelled, correct to 2 decimal places?

answer.worked:
The course makes an angle of $180^{\circ}-156^{\circ}=24^{\circ}$ with south. Let $d$ kilometres be the distance travelled; the southward distance is adjacent to this angle.
$$\begin{align*}
\cos24^{\circ}&=\frac{45}{d}\\
d\cos24^{\circ}&=45\\
d&=\frac{45}{\cos24^{\circ}}\\
d&\approx49.26\text{ km}
\end{align*}$$
